newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March offshore banking unit assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March offshore banking unit assets rise.

text.p: The combined assets of Taiwan's 68 offshore banking units (OBU) grew 14.3 percent to hit a new high of US$38.439 billion at the end of March from a year earlier, the central bank said on Tuesday.
About 78 percent of the assets, held by 37 local banks and 31 foreign banks, came from Asia and the rest from Europe and America, the bank said in a statement.
It added that the bank had recently approved one more OBU application for foreign bank and one more for a local bank.
In March, Taiwan's OBUs reported a monthly foreign exchange turnover of $3.863 billion, the statement said.
Of the derivatives operated by the OBUs, interest rate swaps took $414 million, options took $216 million, financial futures accounted for $66 million and margin trading accounted for $42 million.

The government has planned to expand the OBU business as part of its scheme to become a regional financial centre. This expansion, although its size is currently unspecified, would herald some tax burden for OBUs, officials have said.
